title: Submultiplicativity conjecture for the primitive-set ratio function
source: Nathan McNew, “Counting primitive subsets and other statistics of the divisor graph of {1,...,n}”, arXiv:1808.04923 (2018). (https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.04923), Conjecture 1

lanes.final_paper_definition_and_prior_art_che: final-paper-check-340107-346782-372803-opus-20261119-r1/CHECK-340107.md, PASS WITH EDITORIAL EDITS; revised paper used (Claude Opus 5.5)

significance.root_decision: Let Q(k) be the number of primitive subsets of {1,...,k} (no element divides another; the empty set is counted, as in OEIS A051026) and g(k) = Q(k)/Q(k-1) - 1, with g(1) = 1. Then g(nm) <= g(n) g(m) for coprime n, m >= 1, and g(p^(i+1)) <= g(p^i) for every prime p and i >= 0. This is McNew's Conjecture 1. The proof uses an antichain-avoidance monotonicity lemma (an FKG-type correlation inequality) and two block reductions.
significance.caveat: Modest: about a page using a correlation inequality; a specialist in correlation inequalities might find it quickly, but it is not a corollary of a published theorem. Bounded literature search only. The prior-work paragraph of the paper still refers to internal review files and should be tidied before external use.
